Q: Modeling bounded polymorphic children in SQLite/Drizzle: JSON column vs. Concrete Table Inheritance A:

Keep in mind that tables don't have performance. They just sit there, storing data.

Queries have performance.

Which means before you can make a decision based on the performance implications of using JSON vs. normalized tables, you must know which queries your application needs to execute, and which of these queries you need to be optimized.

Using JSON and merging multi-valued data into one column seems like it's saving something, right? But many kinds of queries are more difficult and harder to optimize when you use JSON. So I recommend that you prototype the queries you need before making a decision to refactor your tables into JSON.

I've answered questions about using JSON in SQL in the past here on Stack Overflow. You might like to go review some of my answers to see examples of how much more difficult SQL queries can become.

I wrote a presentation How to Use JSON in MySQL Wrong (that presentation is about MySQL, not SQLite, but some similar issues exist in SQLite).

I also wrote a chapter about JSON in my book More SQL Antipatterns. The examples in that book use PostgreSQL, but I intended the principles to be applicable to any SQL implementation.

Q: gitlab-runner's git clone fails with "Problem with the SSL CA cert (path? access rights?)" A:

If you have that in a (Docker) container (e.g. Debian Trixy) it may also be possible that the ca certificates (package) is missing. For me, strangely apt works (likely because it does not use HTTPS), but curl/wget/git fails.

So simply doing apt install ca-certificates may solve the issue. For a container, the recommend options/way is:

RUN apt-get update \
      && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
           ca-certificates \
      && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

Q: How to use file and .assets files in a unity project? A:

If files are in a DLL and cant be decompiled into readable assembly code, the code was probably meant to be kept away from prying eyes. The same applies to .asset files, these files are encrypted, you will only decrypt them with a key that the owner of these files holds, if you're determined you could search for the key that makes these files readable from the original source, but it's not advised you try this and may be illegal, check the usability of these assets and Dll's. If it's legal to use these, you could try to decode the DLL with http://unity3d.netobf.com/Unity3dObfuscatorSetup.exe. If the asset files are not encrypted you could rename .assets to .asset and then in Unity just import new asset to access all of the models, textures, etc. Not all assets are obtainable but most of them are. This information came from this unity thread
